message.content:
Below are two ways you can create a Google Compute Engine instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1.  Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Authenticate (if you haven’t already)
gcloud auth login
gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID   # replace with your GCP project ID

# 2️⃣  Enable the Compute Engine API (once per project)
gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com

# 3️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000 \
  --zone us-central1-a \                                 # pick a zone that supports A6000 GPUs
  --machine-type n1-standard-8 \                         # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
  --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \        # 1 RTX A6000
  --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \                       # Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
  --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \                      # official Ubuntu image project
  --boot-disk-size 100GB \                               # size of the boot disk
  --boot-disk-type pd-ssd \                              # SSD persistent disk
  --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
    apt-get update
    apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535   # install the matching driver
    nvidia-smi' \                                 # verify GPU
  --scopes cloud-platform \                            # give full access (or restrict as needed)
  --no-address \                                       # no external IP (optional)
  --quiet
```

### What this does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | The Compute Engine zone that offers the RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs and 30 GB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. `type=nvidia-tesla-a6000` is the official GPU type name. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu project. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | Size and type of the boot disk. |
| `--metadata startup-script` | Runs a shell script after the instance boots. Here it installs the NVIDIA driver and runs `nvidia-smi` to confirm the GPU is visible. |
| `--scopes cloud-platform` | Grants the instance full access to GCP APIs (you can restrict this if you prefer). |
| `--no-address` | Skips assigning an external IP address (useful for private‑only workloads). |
| `--quiet` | Suppresses prompts. |

> **Tip:** If you want the instance to be accessible from the internet, remove `--no-address` or add `--address` to reserve a static external IP.

---

## 2.  Using the REST API (curl)

If you prefer to use the raw REST API, you can POST a JSON payload to the Compute Engine endpoint. Below is a minimal example that you can adapt.

```bash
# 1️⃣  Get an access token (once per session)
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# 2️⃣  Define variables
PROJECT=YOUR_PROJECT_ID
ZONE=us-central1-a
INSTANCE_NAME=my-rtx-a6000
MACHINE_TYPE=n1-standard-8
GPU_TYPE=nvidia-tesla-a6000
IMAGE_FAMILY=ubuntu-2004-lts
IMAGE_PROJECT=ubuntu-os-cloud
BOOT_DISK_SIZE_GB=100

# 3️⃣  Build the JSON body
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_BODY <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/$MACHINE_TYPE",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/$IMAGE_PROJECT/global/images/family/$IMAGE_FAMILY",
        "diskSizeGb": $BOOT_DISK_SIZE_GB,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/$GPU_TYPE"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\\napt-get update\\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\\nnvidia-smi"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ]
}
EOF

# 4️⃣  Make the API call
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_BODY"
```

### What this does

- **`machineType`**: Specifies the CPU/RAM configuration.
- **`disks[0].initializeParams.sourceImage`**: Uses the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image family.
- **`accelerators`**: Adds one RTX A6000 GPU.
- **`metadata.items[0]`**: Runs a startup script that installs the NVIDIA driver and verifies the GPU.
- **`serviceAccounts`**: Grants the instance the default service account with full cloud‑platform scope.

> **Note:** The REST API requires you to handle authentication yourself (here we use `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token`). You can also use a service account key file and exchange it for a bearer token via OAuth 2.0.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Verify that the chosen zone (`us-central1-a` in the examples) actually offers the RTX A6000 GPU. |
| ✅ | Ensure the Compute Engine API is enabled for your project. |
| ✅ | Make sure you have sufficient quota for GPUs in the selected zone. |
| ✅ | Install the correct NVIDIA driver (`nvidia-driver-535` is the current driver that supports RTX A6000). |
| ✅ | If you need external access, either remove `--no-address` or add a static external IP. |
| ✅ | Adjust `--machine-type` and `--boot-disk-size` to match your workload’s CPU, RAM, and storage needs. |

That’s it! Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and run `nvidia-smi` to confirm the GPU is visible and the driver is installed.
